# Firmware

Target: STM32F103C8T6 (Blue Pill), STM32CubeIDE + HAL.

## Why this isn't a full CubeIDE project checked in

USB-CDC, SPI, and I2C peripheral initialization code is normally
**generated by STM32CubeMX**, not hand-written -- ST's USB middleware
in particular is thousands of lines you should not write by hand and
would not add anything to your resume by having written. The files in
this folder are the **application logic** that plugs into a CubeMX-
generated project, not a replacement for one.

## Setup steps

1. Create a new STM32CubeIDE project for STM32F103C8T6.
2. In CubeMX (or the .ioc editor inside CubeIDE), enable:
   - USB peripheral -> Device (FS), then USB_DEVICE middleware ->
     Class: Communication Device Class (Virtual Port Com)
   - SPI1 -> Full-Duplex Master, enable on PA5/PA6/PA7, and configure
     PA4 as a plain GPIO output (software-controlled CS -- do NOT use
     hardware NSS mode, you want manual control for the DAC's timing)
   - I2C1 -> enable on PB6/PB7, Standard Mode 100kHz is plenty
   - GPIO -> PC13 as output (onboard LED)
3. Generate the code. This produces `Core/Src/main.c`,
   `USB_DEVICE/App/usbd_cdc_if.c`, etc.
4. Drop the driver/parser files from this folder's `Core/Src` and
   `Core/Inc` into the generated project's matching folders (they'll
   merge alongside, not replace, CubeMX's generated files).
5. Wire up the one integration point: in the generated
   `usbd_cdc_if.c`, inside `CDC_Receive_FS()`, append received bytes
   to a line buffer and call `SCPI_ProcessLine()` (declared in
   `scpi_parser.h`) whenever a `\n` is received. That's the entire
   USB integration -- everything else in this folder is
   hardware-agnostic application code.

## File overview

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dac_driver.c/.h` | MCP4922 SPI driver -- set output voltage |
| `ina219_driver.c/.h` | INA219 current sensor driver over I2C |
| `ads1115_driver.c/.h` | ADS1115 precision ADC driver over I2C (Kelvin voltage sense) |
| `sweep_engine.c/.h` | Orchestrates a voltage sweep, streams results |
| `scpi_parser.c/.h` | Parses incoming SCPI-style command lines, dispatches to the above |
| `main.c` | Skeleton showing init order and where CubeMX's generated main loop calls into this code |

## A note on calibration constants

`dac_driver.c` and `ina219_driver.c` both have `#define`s for reference
voltage and shunt resistance near the top of the file -- **measure your
actual reference voltage and shunt value with a multimeter once the
board is built** and update these. Off-the-shelf resistors and
regulators have tolerance; this five-minute step is what makes the
difference between "roughly works" and "matches a multimeter to three
digits," which is exactly the kind of detail worth mentioning in an
interview.
